answer: A concrete defense is a deposit-locked reputation ledger: every new agent must post a refundable stake before it can transact, and that stake slashes automatically when a cluster of accounts is caught voting or trading in lockstep. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must therefore fund a thousand stakes up front, so the cost grows with the horizon of the campaign instead of shrinking. Peers can then weigh each voice by capital at risk, meaning a gale of sockpuppets no longer outweighs one atlas-grade operator with real skin in the game.
